title: Dimethyltryptamine and the Recursive Reorganization of Consciousness
object_of_study: DMT-induced reorganization of a brain-body-environment system and subsequent recovery
main_question: How can the rapid multilevel reorganization produced by DMT be structurally separated into departure, altered-state organization, recurrence, and recovery without collapsing phenomenology, mechanism, and ontology into one claim?

claim_layers.claim: The paper integrates evidence across pharmacokinetics, receptor signaling, cellular gain modulation, whole-brain dynamics, embodied physiology, phenomenology, memory, environment, repeated exposure, recovery, and post-session updating (Zenodo record description).

The paper's central formal contribution is a prospective dual-reference architecture distinguishing departure from waking organization from approach toward a candidate recurrent DMT-state organization, treating lockout as a typed outcome and distinguishing local recovery from canonical waking return.

Breakthrough is defined provisionally as sustained altered-reference dominance rather than dose, intensity, neural complexity, visual effects, or ego dissolution — stated by the source as procedurally specified but empirically unvalidated.
